newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portugal hopes EU's Tabaqueira sale fears over.
newsitem.headline: Portugal hopes EU's Tabaqueira sale fears over.

text.p: Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said on Monday he believed the European Commission was no longer concerned about the sale of tobacco firm Tabaqueira to a consortium led by U.S. firm Philip Morris.

Mateus said the privatisation in December of 65 percent of Tabaqueira had not been raised at a meeting with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, but he thought that the Commission's fears about the deal had been overcome.
Van Miert wrote to the Portuguese government at the end of last year expressing concerns about Philip Morris's reinforced position in Portugal after acquiring control of Tabaqueira.
Mateus told reporters that all necessary measures had been taken to avoid creation of "structural barriers to new market entrants both on the production and distribution" sides of the sector.
Van Miert's spokesman could only confirm that the issue had not been raised at the meeting.

Philip Morris controls 80 percent of the consortium which paid 33 billion escudos for the majority stake in Tabaqueira. The Commission has in the past also expressed concerns about Philip Morris's strong position in the Italian market.
